title: Runes: the npm package ships no grammar bytes, so every consumer builds 11 of 23 grammars from source after a toolchain download of about 940 MB
claim: At v1.1.0 the package holds the recipe and the pins (grammars/manifest.json and four patches), no .wasm and no node-types.json. A consumer that parses anything runs buildGrammars; 11 of the 23 pins (typescript, tsx, java, csharp, cpp, php, ruby, json, kotlin, yaml, toml) are source builds, and tree-sitter build --wasm fetches binaryen (302M) and wasi-sdk (638M) into ~/.cache/tree-sitter on its first run. The built grammars take 24M. A source build is refused on Windows.
evidence: npm pack --dry-run --json at v1.1.0: 162 files, 458,121 bytes, no .wasm or node-types.json; du -sh ~/.cache/tree-sitter/* after a first build: 302M binaryen, 638M wasi-sdk; du -sh ~/.cache/runes/grammars: 24M
proposal: Decide how a consumer gets the pinned grammars without compiling them: ship the 23 built files (24M, each named by its sha256 in the manifest) in the package or a companion, or publish them as release assets that buildGrammars already knows how to download and verify; the manifest's sha256 keeps the check as it is.

title: Runes: classifyUse gives no reason for a use in C, C++ or Ruby, so a consumer cannot tell #include <stdio.h> from a missing local header, or require 'json' from a missing require_relative
claim: For a path use in C, C++ and Ruby that binds no file, classifyUse answers {"kind":"absent"} with no reason, where Python gives outside. explainMiss answers for TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, PHP and Rust only, and a symbol hint of any other language reads as no reason. docs/api.md says so and says C, C++ and Ruby may gain reasons.
evidence: classify-use-c-ruby.mjs on v1.1.0 over a listed view: c missing.h, c stdio.h, cpp vector, cpp missing.hpp, ruby json and ruby ./missing each printed {"kind":"absent"}; python os printed {"kind":"absent","reason":"outside"}
proposal: Add outside, unfollowed and unowned for C and C++ (a system include or a header no file of the repository and no include path binds, against a quoted include of the repository) and for Ruby (a require of a gem or the standard library, against a require_relative or a constant of the repository), as additive values of the optional reason field.

title: Runes, Java: a bare nested type inherited from a library supertype (Entry in a class that extends AbstractMap) is answered unfollowed by classifyUse, where the written Map.Entry is outside
claim: The candidates of such a use are java.util.AbstractMap+Entry and the same-package name; keyReason returns pass for both (the inherited reading's level is outside the repository, its separator is +, and the package is the repository's), and classifyUse falls to unfollowed. In google/gson at a961b0fe088f, 14 of the 20 unfollowed uses have this shape: 12 bare Entry in LinkedTreeMap.java, one in MapTest.java:411 and one Context in LegacyProtoTypeAdapterFactoryTest.java:452. On a repository of one class that extends AbstractMap, the written Map.Entry is outside and the bare Entry is unfollowed.
evidence: java-inherited-nested-type.mjs on v1.1.0 over gson: uses 10675, resolved 3092, absent:outside 7563, absent:unfollowed 20; over the one-class repository: src/app/Tree.java:8 java.util.AbstractMap+Entry | app.Entry unfollowed, uses 4 with 3 outside and 1 unfollowed
proposal: When a use's only readings are an inherited member type of a type outside the repository and the repository's own package, and the repository's package declares no type of that name, answer outside; the reading of the same-package name stays unfollowed where the package does declare it.
